overview: First live HackerOne engagement — Nextcloud cognitive run. Deploy local Docker Nextcloud instance, run Raphael cognitive loop (recon → technique proposal → execution), validate end-to-end kill chain against real-world PHP/MySQL web application.

why_nextcloud.stack_alignment: PHP/MySQL/Apache matches Raphael STACK_MAP (file_upload, lfi, sqli, idor)
why_nextcloud.attack_surface: File handling, sharing links (IDOR), authentication, user management
why_nextcloud.non_critical: File sync platform — not financial/healthcare, low regulatory risk

phase_1_recon.objective: Profile target stack, identify running services, extract version info

phase_2_technique_proposal.objective: Generate candidate techniques matching Nextcloud stack

phase_3_execution.objective: Execute authorized candidates, collect evidence, flag findings

phase_4_reflection.objective: Persist lessons learned, update Student KB, identify gaps

rate_limiter.reason: Respectful pacing for live web application

safety_invariants: SI-H1-01: ScopeParser must DENY if target not in 172.18.0.0/16
SI-H1-02: RateLimiter jitter must be 10-20s minimum
SI-H1-03: No destructive actions (DELETE, DROP, FORMAT, SHUTDOWN)
SI-H1-04: All http responses stored as Evidence with trust_level=TOOL_OBSERVATION
SI-H1-05: Flag findings must include HTTP status, body snippet, and evidence_id
SI-H1-06: Max 20 actions per engagement (rate-limited to ~5-10 minutes)
SI-H1-07: Any 5xx response triggers CapabilityBroker review
expected_kill_chain: 1. Recon: http_headers → Nextcloud version, Apache/PHP versions
2. Technique proposal: Student proposes file_upload_shell, lfi_rfi, sqli, idor
3. Upload test: Attempt file upload via /remote.php/dav/files/ (WebDAV)
4. LFI test: Attempt path traversal in file preview endpoint
5. IDOR test: Attempt share link enumeration
7. Evidence collection: All findings stored in WorldModel + EvidenceGraph
8. Reflection: Student KB updated with Nextcloud-specific results
